body.statement:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) satisfy \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and suppose a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied for every source-consistent recorded stratum. There is a universal \(a>0\) such that a randomized localized geometric-resolution algorithm returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). Its arithmetic construction time and certificate length are at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\). In particular, for any fixed \(b>0\), if \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then the bound is \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\) depending only on \(a\) and \(b\). The output polynomial is the monic minimal polynomial over \(K_G\), not a whole-fiber eliminant, and \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) contains the covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-infinity, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits whose nonzero product is \(h_{G,e}\). The theorem is conditional on the supplied charts; it does not construct or select them.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a source-consistent recorded stratum and use the notation in \(\mathrm{def:source\mbox{-}prime\mbox{-}chart}\). Validity gives
\[
P K_G[x]_{H\Delta}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta},
\qquad
\xi(H\Delta)\neq0.
\]
Thus the localized equations define exactly the source prime on the indicated principal open set, rather than an extensional union containing unidentified components. Because the sequence is reduced and regular and \(\Delta\) is nonzero at the source generic point, the Jacobian criterion makes this open set smooth of pure dimension
\[
q=r-c\leq2k.
\]
Adjoining a variable \(z\) and the equation \(zH\Delta-1=0\) converts the inequation to an equation without changing this principal open set.

Over \(\overline{K_G}\), the finitely many conjugates of \(\lambda_e\) are the roots of its separable minimal polynomial, since the characteristic is zero. Each embedding of \(K_G(\lambda_e)\) into \(\overline{K_G}\) extends to a geometric component of the base change of the source prime. The element \(H\Delta\), being nonzero in that prime and defined over \(K_G\), is nonzero on every conjugate component. For any one such component, the affine hyperplanes that meet it properly and nontrivially form a nonempty Zariski-open set. Intersecting these finitely many open sets and applying \(q\) successive hyperplane sections gives affine linear forms \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q\) for which the localized slice is nonempty and zero-dimensional on every conjugate component. Transversality is also open, so the choices may be made so that the sliced algebra is reduced.

The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\) now hold for each chart slice. Its geometric-resolution algorithm produces a finite reduced \(K_G\)-algebra \(B\), multiplication matrices for the exposed coordinates, and the supplied lifting circuits recover every eliminated directed coordinate and the query. Let \(M_e\) be multiplication by \(\lambda_e\) in \(B\), and let
\[
\chi_e(t)=\det(tI-M_e).
\]
Every geometric point of \(B\) lies on the base change of the source prime, hence its queried coordinate is a conjugate of \(\lambda_e\). Conversely, the simultaneous choice of slices meets every conjugate component, so every root of \(p_e\) occurs among the eigenvalues of \(M_e\). Therefore the squarefree part of \(\chi_e\) has exactly the roots of \(p_e\). Both are monic and \(p_e\) is separable, whence
\[
p_e(t)=\operatorname{sqfree}(\chi_e(t)),
\qquad
d_e(G)=\deg p_e.
\]
This equality is the coordinate-projection step: multiplicities and the cardinality of the sliced full fiber do not enter the reported degree.

All coefficients of the chart, multiplication matrices, and lifting maps are elements of \(K_G\) represented by rational covariance circuits. Determinants, greatest common divisors with derivatives, and monic normalization therefore produce coefficientwise rational circuits for \(p_e\). The equality of the localized chart with the source prime ensures that no factor from another incidence component enters \(\chi_e\); source-parametric identity tests certify every zero identity and every proposed nonzero factor. Homogenizing before slicing records the leading forms whose vanishing would create a point at projective infinity. Clearing each rational lifting formula records its pole and incidence-lifting factors. The leading coefficient of the specialized eliminant and its discriminant or squarefreeness resultant are again finite rational covariance circuits. By \(\mathrm{lem:effective\mbox{-}real\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\), the existential predicate that a real root extends through the original supported residual equations has an equivalent finite Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions; by \(\mathrm{lem:real\mbox{-}algebraic\mbox{-}sampling}\), the required exact univariate representations and component sample points can be produced after an algebraic specialization. The elimination and sign polynomials occurring in these two constructions are the real-lifting circuits. Collecting all these factors gives \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and removing repeated nonzero factors from their product gives a nonzero \(h_{G,e}\). The established incidence-localization theorem ensures that these bookkeeping operations do not invert an undeclared directed-coordinate expression.

The arbitrary-equation and inequation machinery in \(\mathrm{lem:lifting\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}equidimensional\mbox{-}decomposition}\) bounds the lifting-fiber operations for the recorded strata, while the reduced-chart solver controls each regular slice. By their cited complexity bounds, multiplication-matrix linear algebra, and the fact that every chart has at most \(2k\) exposed variables, there is a universal \(a>0\) for which the total number of arithmetic operations and output gates is at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Every randomized choice is tested by a displayed nonzero chart, transversality, leading-form, or resultant circuit. Allocating the error budget across the finitely many calls and applying \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\) gives total symbolic error at most \(\delta\).

If \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then, after increasing constants to cover \(n\geq2\),
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a
\leq n^{2ab(k+1)+a(k+1)}
\leq n^{C(k+1)}
\]
for a constant \(C\) depending only on \(a,b\). This is the asserted fixed-parameter corollary.

The cited algorithms do not remove the antecedent. The Gröbner-free algorithm assumes a reduced regular sequence off an inequation. The lifting-fiber algorithm accepts arbitrary equations and inequations, but outputs all relevant equidimensional components and charges the possibly unbounded intermediate geometric degree. Neither marks which component is the embedded source prime, constructs a source-nonzero Jacobian minor for it, or descends an implicitly presented component to bounded rational circuits over \(K_G\). Source identity testing verifies a proposed chart but does not manufacture one. Hence the conclusion proved here is conditional exactly as stated.
body.justification: A valid localized reduced source-prime chart is sufficient for exact coordinate minimal-polynomial and specialization-certificate construction.
body.gap: Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy and Lecerf do not select or descend the embedded SEM source prime, and their complexity retains geometric-degree dependence.
body.consumer: This is the exact higher-degree polynomial-output contract for a chart-certified extension of fasttreeid.
